episode.title: Lighting Decisions That Save a Shoot

feed.description: Photography conversations: craft, storytelling, workflow, and making images under real constraints.
feed.title: Frame & Light

bullets: The first decision in commercial lighting is whether to sharpen existing light rather than rebuild it — framing reveals which tradeoffs are being made.
Color temperature mistakes cost more shoots than focus mistakes, making it the higher-priority failure mode to guard against.
A debt-based heuristic — lighting to solve a percentage of commercial problems — simplifies downstream decisions once internalized.
The second-order effects of lighting choices are the part most people miss, even when the primary tradeoff is visible.
Adopting tools like Adobe or Capture One in the workflow makes tradeoffs visible, but the framing itself determines which tradeoffs matter.
The failure mode in pro photo lighting is harder to spot than in other contexts, so the framing must expose it explicitly.
A practical takeaway: pick one of the recovered EDAOs and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration.
